notice: Light news day — several of the window's bigger stories were already covered in issues 1 and 2, so this edition is slimmer than usual.

lead.title: LM Studio 0.4.22 adds speculative-decoding drafters and tool-image support
lead.summary: The local inference GUI's 0.4.22 update ships DFlash, DSpark, and MTP assistant drafters for speculative decoding (requiring llama.cpp 2.29.1+), alongside support for images returned by tools in OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs. A batch of Linux AppImage/.deb fixes rounds out the release. A directly usable speedup for daily local inference.

top_stories.title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 2: 78 TOPS of entry-level edge AI
top_stories.summary: NVIDIA's next robotics/edge-AI computer doubles the Orin Nano Super's inference performance in the same footprint at 40% lower power, enough for on-device LLMs like Gemma 4 and Qwen 3. Module and dev kit ship H1 2027.

top_stories.title: Pinea Pi debuts edge AI nodes with up to 275 TOPS for offline inference
top_stories.summary: The new line targets local robotics and embodied-AI workloads: the Pi Pro carries 275 TOPS of NVIDIA compute while the Pi Lite packs up to 180 TOPS of Intel performance, both running fully offline with a privacy switch. Kickstarter launches late September.

top_stories.title: AgentBridge: one agent thinks while another writes the code
top_stories.summary: A new open-source Rust agent harness that splits reasoning from code-writing across two models, debuted on Show HNable and runs locally for multi-model agent workflows.

items.title: QLoRA's acquisition-retention frontier for learning new facts
items.summary: Traces how parameter-efficient fine-tuning trades off acquiring new facts against keeping pretrained capabilities, showing the outcome depends strongly on adapter capacity. A controlled OpenStreetMap-derived benchmark on Qwen3-4B informs adapter-rank choices for consumer-hardware fine-tuning.

items.title: DualOPSD: adaptive privileged teachers for on-policy self-distillation
items.summary: Improves on-policy self-distillation with an asymmetric alternating scheme and adaptive privileged teachers, sharpening dense-supervision distillation for language-model training.

items.title: How much rank does LoRA need? Error bounds for attention heads
items.summary: Offers task-dependent theory for the approximation error achievable at each LoRA rank on Transformer attention heads, providing a principled guide to picking rank instead of pure empirical tuning.

items.title: Itsuki: an open-source memory engine for AI agents with API and MCP
items.summary: A self-hosted memory layer for local AI agents exposing both a plain API and a Model Context Protocol interface, launched on Show HN as the memory layer under agent tooling.

items.title: Metis coding agent reports roughly 50% higher coding performance
items.summary: An agent harness on Show HN that wraps existing coding agents to push results toward Opus-tier scores on local setups, easing multi-agent coding workflows.

items.title: DeepSeekGUI: Windows desktop client for DeepSeek's coding agent
items.summary: A TypeScript desktop app for running DeepSeek's coding agent locally on Windows, wrapping the official web UI with an independent workbench in development.

items.title: NVIDIA GeForce driver 616.56 delivers compute gains via CUDA 13.3
items.summary: The WHQL driver (Aug 26) brings CUDA 13.3 with real inference-relevant uplifts: about +8.1% in path tracing on the RTX 5080chers, +21.7% OpenCL, and +5.5% CUDA in Geekbench 7.

items.title: NVIDIA at Gamescom: DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction and RTX Spark goes Game Ready
items.summary: DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction lands for all GeForce RTX GPUs and NVIDIA confirms its Arm-based RTX Spark AI PC platform is Game Ready this fall, targeting compact desktops and laptops for on-device inference.
